text: Write a program that demonstrates the one integer whose absolute value is negative. Fill in the two blanks.
choices: int n = ___;                       // the value with no positive counterpart
System.out.println(n + " -> " + ___);   // apply the standard library's abs
explanation: Verified: it prints -2147483648 -> -2147483648. `Math.abs` is documented to do this, and the reason is Section 2.2.2's asymmetry — there is no positive 2147483648 in an `int`, so negating MIN_VALUE overflows back to itself. Write it, run it, and note that no exception is thrown. Any code that assumes `Math.abs(x) >= 0` has a bug for exactly one input, which is the hardest kind to find by testing.
